note: Unpack cases for the rules U-01 to U-14 of 03-verifier-contract.md, round 4. These are descriptions, not archives: the producer could run no program and therefore could write no tar.gz file. All of them are shape-only. The implementer builds each archive from the description; 'neighbour' describes the nearest archive that must unpack. In every case the expected outcome also includes: nothing of the archive remains under the final name, and the staging directory of the attempt is removed or reported. Names in U-03 to U-05 mean the EFFECTIVE entry name after pax 'path' records and GNU long-name records are applied; a name record that does not resolve to one effective name refuses under its own rule.

cases.archive: tar.gz with three regular files 'bin/example-manager' (mode 0755), 'LICENSE' and 'README.md' (mode 0644) and one directory entry 'bin/' (a single trailing '/' on a directory entry is allowed by U-05 and is stripped for the component test); total content bytes equal the declared unpacked_size
unpack-valid-01, with one byte of the protected copy changed after the verification record was written
a zip file, or a tar file compressed with a method other than gzip, stored under an artifact whose format is 'tar.gz'
one entry whose effective name is '/etc/example'; a second variant: a plain name with a pax 'path' record that replaces it by an absolute path
one entry whose effective name is '../../.profile'; a second variant: 'bin/../../x'; a third variant: a GNU long-name record that makes the effective name contain '..'

an entry whose effective name has an empty component ('bin//x'), a component '.', a byte outside 0x20 to 0x7e, a backslash, more than 255 bytes, or more than 16 components; a directory entry with two trailing slashes ('bin//') is this code, not the allowed single one
a symbolic link entry 'bin/x' pointing to '/etc/passwd'; a second variant: a symbolic link that stays inside the directory; a third variant: a hard link entry
a character device entry; variants: block device, FIFO, socket, and any tar entry type that is not a regular file or a directory
a regular file entry with the setuid bit; variants: setgid, sticky
a regular file entry with an extended header that carries 'security.capability'; variants: any other extended attribute, a POSIX ACL record

two entries with the same effective name 'bin/example-manager'; a second variant: a file entry 'bin' followed by a file entry 'bin/x'; a third variant: two different raw names whose effective names are equal after a long-name record

content bytes one larger than the declared unpacked_size; a second variant: a small archive of zero-filled content that inflates past the declared unpacked_size (the write stops at the first byte beyond the bound)

cases.neighbour: an archive with 4096 entries whose content fits the declared unpacked_size

cases.archive: unpack-valid-01 followed by a second gzip member or by bytes after the end-of-archive marker
unpack-valid-01 without 'bin/example-manager', while the placement table of the plan names that path for this product

two products, each unpacking cleanly on its own, whose placement rows in the plan name one destination for a file of each; the conflict is between plan rows, and the second product's placement refuses before anything is written to the shared destination
cases.neighbour: the same two products with placement rows that name different destinations

cases.archive: an archive whose total decompressed stream (headers, padding and content together) exceeds the decompressed-stream cap of the limits table while its content bytes stay within the declared unpacked_size; a second variant: one extended-header (pax) record larger than the per-record cap
